name: sol-azy

provenance.install: git clone plus cargo build --release, the only path the project documents. There is NO crate named sol-azy on crates.io: the API returns 404, so the `cargo install radar` trap cannot arise here.
provenance.note: Built with `cargo update -p allocative --precise 0.3.4` because the project gitignores its Cargo.lock and the default resolution fails with two versions of hashbrown in one graph. That changes dependency resolution only: no rule, threshold, argument or source line of the tool was altered, it was decided before any corpus run, and it is recorded in mappings/sol-azy.json under build_note.

run.invocation_evidence: copied from the `cmd` field of raw/c2-sol-azy.json.log, which records the exact docker invocation of all 18 runs behind the sol-azy corpus-2 result

layout_reason: sol-azy decides what a directory is from its contents: helpers/mod.rs get_project_type calls it Anchor only if it holds Anchor.toml and SBF only if its Cargo.toml declares solana-program. sealevel-attacks crates satisfy neither, so all 33 corpus-1 per-case runs exited 0 having read nothing. Same family of trap as radar's, opposite shape.

evidence.means: sol-azy's own count of the files it read. It is exactly this line that separated the 33 corpus-1 runs that read nothing from the runs that worked; without it all 33 would have been zeros.

output.patterns_note: Taken from the runner B3 wrote (run_solazy.py). begin_at exists because sol-azy prints a summary table before the detail section and a parser that reads both counts every finding twice. B3's own pattern additionally required the path to start with a slash, which is true of sol-azy's container output and not of the relative paths this repository stores; the leading slash is not required here so the same pattern reads both, and the parse of the committed artefacts is unchanged, which tools/scanner_spec.py --demo checks against the 36 raw run files.

envelope_note: sol-azy speaks prose, so its findings are stored in the flat sol-audit envelope, which is what B3 did and what raw/c2-sol-azy.json contains. Declared rather than inferred.

positive_control.sample_source: the shape of raw/solazy-2026-09-01/c2/*.txt, with one finding substituted for the fix site of the synthetic case

measurements.off_clock_reason: sol-azy is measured (0 detected of 15 analysed, 1 could not run) but has never been on the clock, and putting it there is a deliberate act somebody should take rather than a side effect of this refactor. B3 also names a trap that must be handled first: run_all.previous() takes the lexicographically last file in runs/, so any file sorting after runs/<today>.json makes the next scheduled run report every existing scanner as `disappeared`.
measurements.note: 0 detected, 0 unlocated, 10 missed, 5 no-rule, 1 not built, 1 could not run (spl-stake-pool-mint-decimals: ~14 GB RSS then killed by the kernel OOM killer, reproducibly, on a 4,011-line processor.rs). Honest denominator 0 of 15 analysed. Run twice on the pinned corpus with byte-identical findings, which is the determinism check passing.
